Ship-phase progressed through verify, secure (27/27 threats closed), SDK E2E gate (caught and fixed a real regression), and CodeRabbit review (7 in-scope fixes applied, 4 todos deferred). repo: Ed25519 IPNS record protobufs do NOT embed the pubKey field — the key lives in the IPNS name (k51…). `parseIpnsRecordBytes` never yields `pubKey`; it must be supplied separately from the DB `publicKey` column, which is validated at publish time via `deriveIpnsName(publicKey) === ipnsName`.

`decode_ipns_cbor_data` rejects duplicate Value/Sequence CBOR keys (documented guard against parser-differential attacks), but `decode_ipns_cbor_validity` previously used first-wins early-return semantics — an asymmetry that exposed a cross-parser ambiguity vector.

`register_device` in `crates/sdk` used `Err(_) => None` catch-all for the 'no existing registry' case, silently treating VerifyError::Invalid (bad sig, tampered record) as legitimate first-device bootstrap. The only correct not-found signal is `ApiError::IpnsNotFound` (HTTP 404).

`parse_rfc3339_to_unix_secs` in api-client had two leniency gaps: no iterator exhaustion check (trailing components like '2026-01-01-99' accepted), and day validation only checked 1–31, allowing impossible dates (2026-02-31) that the Hinnant civil_from_days algorithm silently rolls forward into a later expiry — the opposite of fail-closed.

The `(D-XX)` notation in commit subject lines (e.g. `feat(60-01): ... (D-07)`) violates the repo's `subject-no-parens` commitlint rule and breaks the Release Please `pr-release-preview` CI gate on versioned packages.

`lint-staged` only processes TS/JSON/MD files — Rust files are committed as-is without formatting enforcement. `cargo fmt --check` reports workspace-wide drift due to local rustfmt version mismatch vs the repo style; never run `cargo fmt` blindly.
The GSD commit helper (`gsd_run query commit`) can return `commit_failed` while the commit actually lands — always verify with `git log --oneline -1`, never blindly retry.
`gh pr edit` is blocked on this repo due to Projects-classic GraphQL; patch PR body via `gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file` instead.

code.finding: 60-05's D-06 enrich removal left resolveRecord returning the bare network result (from parseIpnsRecordBytes) on equal-seq, which lacks pubKey and signatureV2 fields. The strict client correctly threw fail-closed on every publish→resolve round-trip. Fix: serve the authoritative DB cachedResult (which carries the full signed record + pubKey column) instead of the network result.

parseCachedRecord must supply pubKey from the DB `publicKey` column — Ed25519 record protobufs don't carry it. Missing pubKey caused the strict client to throw on every resolve. Added fail-closed guard: throw if publicKey column is absent rather than returning an incomplete record.

TS resolve path skipped the entire EOL block when Validity was not a Uint8Array (i.e. absent), silently accepting records with no Validity. Rust fail-closed on absent Validity via .ok_or_else(). Fixed: mirror Rust — throw when Validity field is absent.

decode_ipns_cbor_validity used early-return first-wins semantics for duplicate CBOR Validity keys. Its sibling decode_ipns_cbor_data explicitly rejects duplicates (documented cross-parser attack guard). Fixed to accumulate and reject duplicates, mirroring the sibling's pattern.

register_device's broad `Err(_) => None` treated ALL errors including verification failures as 'no registry yet', triggering first-device auto-authorization on tampered/invalid records. Fixed to only bootstrap on `SdkError::Api(ApiError::IpnsNotFound)`; all other errors propagate.

parse_rfc3339_to_unix_secs had two leniencies: (1) date/time component iterators not checked for exhaustion, accepting trailing junk; (2) day validated only as 1–31, allowing month-overflow dates (2026-02-31) that Hinnant algorithm rolls forward into later expiry — violating fail-closed EOL enforcement.
Verify cache had no size bound, risking unbounded memory growth under high publish volume. Added LRU-style eviction at a configured maximum entry count.
Web vault-settings sequence fallback swallowed verification errors (broad catch treated them as not-found). Fixed to propagate non-404 errors fail-closed.

60-05's own unit test (`D-06: enrich removed`) codified the bug by asserting signatureV2/data are undefined on equal-seq. The test mocked parseIpnsRecord to include pubKey (which real Ed25519 records don't carry), masking the round-trip break. Updated to assert the corrected strict-verifiable behavior.

workflow: The SDK E2E gate is the only suite exercising the real client→API IPNS publish/resolve round-trip. Unit suites (Rust 351, sdk-core 252, API jest 173) all mock the resolve boundary and missed the 60-05 regression entirely — SDK E2E caught 28/89 failures that would have shipped broken.

Adversarial triage workflows are effective for high-finding-count reviewer outputs: 15 CodeRabbit findings → 7 fix-now, 4 defer-todo, 4 skip-false-positive, each verified against current code rather than accepted at face value.

Sequential gsd-executor subagents on the feature branch (vs worktree-isolated parallel agents) is the correct mode for security-critical phases with cross-plan compile dependencies — parallel isolation requires a merge protocol the harness doesn't reliably support.
Stale mid-edit diagnostic snapshots from subagents can report false compile errors. Always run authoritative `cargo check` after subagent completion before concluding there is a build failure.

When a background Bash chain is backgrounded, later commands in the chain may not complete before the process is read — verify each commit group individually rather than chaining all in one background invocation.

The 1Password SSH agent wedges after rapid-fire signing sessions (`op-ssh-sign: failed to fill whole buffer`). Recovery: quit and reopen 1Password desktop app, or toggle Settings → Developer → SSH agent off/on. Agent key listing still works even when signing is broken.

friction: 1Password SSH signer wedged mid-session blocking all commits; required user intervention to restart the app before work could continue.
GSD commit helper emits false-negative `commit_failed` on nearly every commit, requiring `git log --oneline -1` verification after every commit attempt.
Background Bash chains get cut off when backgrounded — TS commits in a single backgrounded chain had to be retried individually.
`cargo fmt --check` reports workspace-wide formatting drift due to local rustfmt version mismatch, making it impossible to use as a pre-commit check without spuriously reformatting the entire repo.
No worktree manifest exposed to the harness — parallel worktree subagents cannot reliably merge back, forcing sequential execution and losing the wall-clock benefit of wave parallelism.
The Cargo.lock from 60-01 was not committed by the executor (Wave 1), discovered only at Wave 2's Rust gate check — a latent `--locked` CI break that had to be committed manually.
60-01-SUMMARY.md got a stale self-check footer appended after its commit (in a separate executor pass), requiring manual revert.
`gh pr edit` is blocked on this repo — all PR body patches require a raw `gh api -X PATCH` workaround.
